title: Expose Variables to Blueprints
description: Add UPROPERTY variables to a C++ class and test editing in the editor.
problemStatement:
**Goal:** Make a C++ class configurable in the editor and Blueprints.

1. Create a new C++ Actor `ConfigurableActor`.
2. Add a UPROPERTY float `Speed` with specifiers `EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category = "Movement"`. Default 600.0f.
3. Add a UPROPERTY bool `bIsActive` with `EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category = "State"`. Default true.
4. In `BeginPlay`, log the values:
   ```cpp
   UE_LOG(LogTemp, Warning, TEXT("Speed: %f, Active: %d"), Speed, bIsActive);
   ```
5. Compile. Place the actor in a level. Select it and see the Categories in Details. Change values.
6. Play and verify the log shows the changed values.

**Expect:** The properties appear in the editor, can be modified per instance, and affect runtime behavior.
hints: If properties don't show up, make sure you used the correct specifiers and compiled successfully.
Use Category to group related properties – helps designers.
expectedOutput: Editable properties in Details panel, reflected in game log.
